CORAM: - Hon'ble Mr. Justice Rongon Mukhopadhyay Hon'ble Mr. Justice Ambuj Nath ------

For the Appellant : Mr. A. K. Kashyap, Sr. Advocate For the State : Mr. Manoj Kr. Mishra, A.P.P.
------
04/09.07.2025 I.A. No. 6263 of 2025 Heard Mr. A. K. Kashyap, learned senior counsel for the appellant and Mr. Manoj Kr. Mishra, learned A.P.P. for the State.
This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during the pendency of this appeal.

The appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(f) & 376(3) of the I.P.C. and Sections 4 & 6 of the POCSO Act and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years alongwith fine of Rs. 25,000/- for the offences punishable under Sections 4 & 6 of the POCSO Act.
It has been alleged that the appellant had molested the victim and since 27.10.2019 he continued to rape her by showing pornographic videos to her.
Even after reporting the matter to her parents by the victim, no action was taken and the appellant continued to sexually exploit the victim.

Learned senior counsel for the appellant has submitted that as per the victim, the incident had occurred three years prior to the lodging of the F.I.R. and despite reporting the matter to her parents, no action was taken and the appellant continued to giving tuition to her.
It has further been submitted that the dispute had occurred only on account of running a school.

sentences.text: 1 counsel for the appellant has also referred to the medical report of the victim, wherein no internal or external injury was found on the person of the victim though it has been opined that sexual assault upon the victim cannot be ruled out.
1|Page Learned A.P.P has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.

It seems, as per the evidence of the victim who has been examined as P.W.-1, that molestation and rape upon the victim continued for almost three years and even after the matter being reported to her parents, they did not react which resulted in the appellant continuing with his sexual adventures with the victim and there has been no other complaint made by the victim save and except disclosing about the incident to her parents.

On consideration of the fact that the incident continued for almost three years and the medical report of the victim not indicating any internal or external injury found on the private parts of the victim, we are inclined to admit the appellant on bail.

Accordingly, during the pendency of this appeal, appellant, above named, is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.
10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of learned Exclusive Special Judge (POCSO), Gumla in Special POCSO Case No. 76 of 2022 arising out of Gumla P.S. Case No. 316 of 2022.

The aforesaid I.A. stands allowed and disposed of.
(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J) (Ambuj Nath, J) Jay-Rahul/
